decisions.reason: The exact charged Ricci-square identity gives 4q^4/Sigma^4 tending to infinity for q nonzero. Isometry and continuity of curvature contractions of a C2 nondegenerate metric contradict the supplied sequence limit. Sigma tending to zero also forces r to zero and, for a nonzero, theta to pi/2, yielding the stated ring. Repetition of a supplier conclusion is not a logical defect; no change is warranted.

The cited thm-emg-xs-kn-extension is kind theorem, domain mathematics, library mathematics; its 1299-item dependency closure contains no physics-domain supplier. Only the smooth displayed metric and chosen time orientation enter F2. Direct inversion makes d(v-r) timelike uniformly on the compact sphere near the root; the future-null conormal gives dr<=0 there. Smooth normalized causal vectors have bounded radial derivatives on a finite compact patch cover, and the mean-value theorem yields the stated uniform linear bound. No physical premise is used.

For a=0 and M=abs(q)>0 the norm is -(r-M)^2/r^2, so the ergoregion is empty and its relative boundary is empty although r=M is a stationary-limit set. The Statement consistently distinguishes these sets and its rotating strict inequalities are sound off the axis. Only the title overclaimed ergosurfaces; renamed it to stationary-limit set, with the complete Statement and Proof unchanged.

The flux supplier Statement specifies fluxes and finite homologous sphere conservation but does not state closedness; L1 falsely attributes closedness to that exact interface. Nonzero flux alone does not rule out a bounding 3-chain. Added direct mathematical verification and duality suppliers: dF=d(star F)=0 on the full-sphere exterior and constant dual rotation imply dF_beta=0 on the annulus. Finite-chain Stokes now proves nonbounding and nonglobal exactness. The Poincare lemma on convex north/south product charts supplies the retained local-potential conclusion. All draft qualifications and the Example remain unchanged.

FTC I differentiates an integral function and does not justify the asserted monotonicity of an arbitrary differentiable integrating-factor product. This was a load-bearing supplier mismatch in both crossing exclusions. Added cor-mean-value-theorem and checked continuity on closed C1 pieces and differentiability in their interiors: the derivative signs imply the required monotonicities, which patch across the finite partition. Added continuous-implies-integrable for the smooth compact radial integrands used by FTC I. The full angular collar, null-vector identities, positive exterior tangent and one unbounded-radius path prove both inclusions and the relative boundary, including extremality. The Statement is unchanged.
